chunks.text: 22-year-old male, Senior Official or Manager, resident of Choa Chu Kang, Singapore.
Smoking cessation program completed 2 years ago
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms. [Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go over a few things to make sure everything goes smoothly for your laparoscopic appendectomy under general anesthesia with an LMA.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. I'm ready, just a bit nervous lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. Let's start with your current health. Can you tell me a bit about your symptoms and how long you've been having them?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've had tummy pain for about two days, mostly on the right side. It's been getting worse, and I've had some fever and loss of appetite. The doctor said it's appendicitis and needs to come out.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, let's go over your medications. I see you're on Atorvastatin, Omeprazole, and Paracetamol as needed. Can you confirm the current dose of Atorvastatin you're taking?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, yes. I was on 10 mg daily for a while, but my doctor increased it to 20 mg daily about three months ago because my cholesterol levels were still high.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. And how often are you taking the Omeprazole and Paracetamol?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I take Omeprazole every morning, and Paracetamol only when I have pain or fever. I actually stopped taking it a few days ago when the pain started.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Got it. And do you have any allergies we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a rash when I took Penicillin before, so I'm allergic to that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Noted. We'll make sure to avoid Penicillin and related antibiotics. Now, about your health history — you mentioned obesity and hyperlipidemia. Are you managing these well?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I try my best, but with my BMI at 28.5, it's been a struggle. I walk a bit and watch my diet, but I know I need to do more.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's good to hear. Any other medical conditions or recent illnesses?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing else. I haven't been sick recently except for this.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Have you had any anesthesia before? Any issues with it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I've never had surgery before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. And finally, are you NPO as instructed? Nothing by mouth since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I haven't eaten or drunk anything since last night. Just a sip of water for my morning meds.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Thank you for going through all that with me. I'll be with you throughout the surgery and make sure you're comfortable and safe. Any questions before we proceed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thanks, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol two hundred and fifty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA sixteen in place, good seal, capnograph trace confirmed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] fentanyl twenty micrograms intravenous

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] rocuronium fifty milligrams intravenous

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] normal saline one liter fluid bolus administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five mmHg, atropine one milligram intravenous given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:45] desflurane at one point two percent for maintenance

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] surgery completed, LMA removed, patient extubated smoothly

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling a bit groggy, but okay, I guess. Still waking up.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's normal. Can you tell me your pain level on a scale of 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4? There's some discomfort in my tummy, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we'll manage that with some medication. Are you feeling nauseous at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A little, but not throwing up or anything. Just a bit of a queasy feeling.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we'll keep an eye on that. How's your breathing? Any tightness or discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, breathing's fine. My throat's a bit sore, but I can breathe okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That soreness is from the LMA tube. It should ease soon. Any memory of the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. I was out completely.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Given your BMI and hyperlipidemia, we'll monitor your vitals closely. Any chest pain or shortness of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing like that. Just tired and a bit sore.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, rest well. We'll check on you regularly and get you mobilized soon.

22-year-old male presenting with appendicitis, undergoing elective laparoscopic appendectomy under general anesthesia with LMA.

Patient has a history of obesity (BMI 28.5) and hyperlipidemia managed with Atorvastatin 20 mg daily. No recent cardiac assessments or concerns. Patient is NPO since midnight with only a sip of water for morning medications.

Intraoperative course included administration of Propofol, Fentanyl, Rocuronium, and Desflurane. Transient hypotension (MAP 55 mmHg) was treated with Atropine. LMA was removed, and patient was extubated smoothly.

Monitor for airway complications due to obesity. Watch for post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV), especially given obesity and laparoscopic surgery. Manage analgesia considering pre-operative pain and Paracetamol use pattern. Monitor hemodynamics due to intra-operative hypotension. Provide respiratory monitoring post-extubation due to history of smoking and obesity.
Patient reports feeling groggy but okay, with some tummy discomfort and a pain level of 4 on a scale of 1 to 10.
Patient experiences mild nausea, described as a queasy feeling, but no vomiting.
Patient's breathing is fine with no tightness or discomfort, but reports a sore throat from the LMA tube.
Patient has no memory of the surgery, indicating effective anesthesia.
No chest pain or shortness of breath reported, but patient is tired and sore.
Anesthesia management included Propofol 250mg for induction, Fentanyl 20μg, Rocuronium 50mg, and Desflurane 1.2% for maintenance.
Patient received a fluid bolus of Normal Saline 1 liter intraoperatively.
Mean Arterial Pressure dropped to 55 mmHg, managed with Atropine 1mg IV.
LMA 16 was used with a good seal, confirmed by capnograph trace.
Patient was NPO as instructed preoperatively, with only a sip of water for morning medications.
